bullets.text: Combined ratio was 92.4 and net income grew 20%. Commercial Auto lagged projected profitability, partly due to late-emerging claims and high-limit profile volatility, though Progressive sees no need for immediate corrective action.
Written and earned premiums grew 7% and 8%, respectively; unit growth was weaker at 1%–2% for Personal Lines and Commercial Auto, though dynamics began trending more favorably late in Q1.

Agency auto conversion and new applications fell on comparable quote opportunities. Direct auto new applications crossed from below to above prior-year levels, driven largely by Internet and mobile quote interest.

Progressive is satisfied rate levels are close to objectives; significant conversion changes may depend largely on competitors' actions. Renewals, having greater influence on the book, were generally negatively affected by rate increases.

Unfavorable prior accident year development was about $65 million, mostly from Agency Personal Lines and Commercial Auto, partly reflecting that initial frequency and severity estimates for late-emerging BI and PD claims proved too low.

Estimates of policy life expectancy declined notably through late 2012 and Q1 before early reversal signs appeared. Motorcycle new applications also reflected poor March riding conditions and low interest.

Atypical early catastrophe losses arose from late-February and March hail storms across Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, and Georgia, damaging about 16,000 insured vehicles in areas not normally among Progressive's highest hail exposure geographies.

New campaign reframes Snapshot messaging from potential savings to avoiding subsidizing poorer drivers; several thousand agents plugged Snapshot devices into their own vehicles to experience and relay benefits.
Mobile acquisition capabilities expanded to quote almost all combinations of cars and drivers on mobile devices; plans underway to enhance service response to match mobile acquisition success.
Promotional plans developed with American Strategic Insurance for home-auto bundles; opened 55th and 56th Service Centers in Maryland and Pennsylvania, with seven more planned before year-end.
